options.label: Stops when MASTER SWITCH released from START

ge-q2.text: Is the DEAD CRANK switch set to NORMAL?

options.label: No — it was not set to NORMAL

ge-a1.text: Set DEAD CRANK switch to NORMAL
ge-a1.actionText: Set the DEAD CRANK switch to the NORMAL position. Try cranking the engine again.

ge-q3.text: Is the DC CONTROL POWER circuit breaker pushed in (ON)?

ge-a2.text: Push in the DC CONTROL POWER circuit breaker
ge-a2.actionText: The DC CONTROL POWER circuit breaker must be pushed in (energized) before starting (WP 0005, Initial Adjustments). Push it in, then check the Emergency Stop switch (Step 3).

ge-q4.text: Is the Emergency Stop Switch pulled out (released)?

ge-a3.actionText: Pull the Emergency Stop Switch out to release it. Try cranking the engine again.

ge-q5.text: Check the battery connections. Are any loose or corroded? (Step 4)

ge-q6.text: Is the ambient temperature below 40 degrees F?

ge-a5.actionText: Turn the MASTER SWITCH to PREHEAT for a MAXIMUM of 30 seconds, then crank (WP 0005, Starting Procedures). Do not crank more than 15 seconds; let the starter cool at least 15 seconds between attempts.

ge-q6a.text: Does the engine start now after preheating?

ge-q7.text: Check the air cleaner restriction indicator. Is the air cleaner dirty or clogged?

ge-a6.actionText: Shut down. Open the left engine access door. Loosen the wing nut clamp and remove the end cap; remove the wing nut and air cleaner element. If fouled, discard the element and install a new one. Wipe the housing interior with a clean lint-free cloth. Reinstall element, wing nut, and end cap; close the door (WP 0014, Servicing). Try starting again.

ge-q8.text: Is the fuel filter/water separator dirty or full of water?

ge-a7.actionText: Shut down. Rotate MASTER SWITCH to PRIME & RUN. Open the left engine access door, open the fuel drain cock on the fuel filter/water separator and drain contaminants into a container, then close the drain cock. Close the door and rotate MASTER SWITCH to OFF (WP 0017, Servicing). Try starting again.

ge-q10.text: Did you hold the MASTER SWITCH in START until oil pressure reached at least 25 psi (172 kPa), voltage came up, and speed stabilized? (Step 1)

options.label: No — I released it too soon

ge-a8.text: Hold MASTER SWITCH in START longer
ge-a8.actionText: Turn the MASTER SWITCH to START and hold it there. Watch the oil pressure gauge. Do not release until oil pressure reaches at least 25 psi. The engine will shut down if released before oil pressure is sufficient.

ge-q10a.text: Does the engine stay running now?

ge-q12.text: Are any FAULT INDICATOR lights lit? (Symptom 4, Step 1)

ge-q13.text: Is the DC CONTROL POWER circuit breaker de-energized (out)? (Step 2)

ge-q14.text: Check the air cleaner restriction indicator. Is the air cleaner dirty or clogged?

ge-a10.actionText: Service the air cleaner assembly (WP 0014, Servicing): replace a fouled element, wipe the housing clean, reinstall. Restart and check.

ge-q14a.text: Does the engine run smoothly now?

ge-q15.text: Could the fuel be contaminated (water, dirt, or wrong fuel type)?

ge-a11.actionText: Drain contaminants from the fuel filter/water separator with the MASTER SWITCH at PRIME & RUN (WP 0017, Servicing). Restart and check.

ge-q15a.text: Does the engine run smoothly now?

ge-q16.text: Is the generator using the correct fuel type listed for the current temperature in TM WP 0016, Table 1 (e.g. DF-2, DF-1, DF-A, JP-8, JP-5)?

ge-q18.text: Check the air cleaner restriction indicator. Is the air cleaner dirty or clogged?

ge-a12.actionText: Service the air cleaner assembly (WP 0014, Servicing). Run and check power.

ge-q18a.text: Does the generator develop full power now?

ge-a13.actionText: Drain contaminants from the fuel filter/water separator (WP 0017, Servicing). Run and check power.

ge-q19a.text: Does the generator develop full power now?

ge-q20.text: Is the exhaust opening obstructed? (Symptom 6, Step 3)

ge-q21.text: Is the generator using a fuel listed for the current temperature in TM WP 0016, Table 1?

ge-q22.text: Check the oil level on the dipstick. Is the oil low?

ge-a14.actionText: Add oil per LO 9-6115-642-12 (WP 0018, Servicing). Run the engine and listen.

ge-q22a.text: Is the knocking gone after adding oil?

ge-q23.text: Check the engine compartment for loose parts or foreign objects (Symptom 7, Step 2). Any found?

options.label: Yes — found loose parts or foreign objects

ge-a15.text: Loose parts or foreign objects found in the engine compartment (the TM gives no operator action). Do not operate; notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Engine knocks — loose parts/foreign objects in engine compartment

ge-q24.text: Is the generator using a fuel listed for the current temperature in TM WP 0016, Table 1?

ge-t1.text: Engine cranks after setting the DEAD CRANK switch, DC CONTROL POWER breaker, or Emergency Stop switch to the normal starting position (WP 0005, Initial Adjustments).

terminal.summary: Engine fails to crank — DEAD CRANK / DC CONTROL POWER / E-STOP set correctly

ge-t2.text: Engine fails to crank after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Engine fails to crank — beyond operator repair

ge-t3.text: Loose or corroded battery connections: do not clean or tighten them yourself — notify the next higher maintenance level (WP 0009, Symptom 1, Step 4). Battery cables damaged, loose, or missing parts is NMC (WP 0011, Table 1, item 18).

terminal.summary: Engine fails to crank — battery connections loose/corroded, needs maintenance

ge-t4.text: Cold-weather start: PREHEAT (max 30 s) resolved the problem.

terminal.summary: Cold weather — PREHEAT (max 30 s) used, engine started

ge-t5.text: Air cleaner was dirty. Serviced and engine runs properly.

terminal.summary: Dirty air cleaner — serviced, engine runs properly

ge-t6.text: Engine cranks but will not start after preheat, air cleaner, and fuel filter/water separator service. Notify the next higher maintenance level (WP 0009, Symptom 2, Step 3).

terminal.summary: Engine cranks but won't start — needs maintenance

ge-t7.text: Fuel filter/water separator serviced. Engine runs properly.

terminal.summary: Fuel filter/water separator dirty — serviced, engine runs

ge-t8.text: Engine stops when the MASTER SWITCH is released, with a fault light other than NO FUEL or with no cause found. Notify the next higher maintenance level (WP 0009, Symptom 3).

terminal.summary: Engine stops on switch release — needs maintenance

ge-t9.text: Engine stays running. Operator was releasing MASTER SWITCH too early.

terminal.summary: Improper starting procedure — held START until 25 psi

ge-t11.text: Engine stops suddenly with a fault light (other than NO FUEL) or no operator-level cause. Notify the next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Engine stops suddenly — needs maintenance

ge-t12.text: Engine stopped suddenly and the DC CONTROL POWER circuit breaker is out. Do not reset it — notify the next higher maintenance level (WP 0009, Symptom 4, Step 2).

terminal.summary: Engine stopped — DC CONTROL POWER breaker tripped, needs maintenance

ge-t13.text: Wrong fuel type in the generator. Notify next higher maintenance level to drain and refuel with correct fuel.

terminal.summary: Improper fuel type — needs drain and refuel

ge-t14.text: Engine runs erratically after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Engine runs erratically — beyond operator repair

ge-t16.text: Generator does not develop full power after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Low power output — beyond operator repair

ge-t17.text: Oil was low causing engine knock. Oil added, knock resolved.

terminal.summary: Low oil caused knock — oil added, knock resolved

ge-t19.text: Engine knocks after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Engine knock — beyond operator repair

ge-q11.text: Are any FAULT INDICATOR lights lit? (Step 2)

ge-a16.actionText: WARNING: fuel is explosive — no smoking or open flame. Shut down, remove the fuel cap, clean the strainer as necessary, and add the specified diesel fuel (WP 0016, Table 1); install the cap (WP 0016, Servicing). Restart.

ge-q11a.text: Does the engine start and keep running with the NO FUEL light out?

ge-t20.text: Out of fuel (NO FUEL light). Refueled and the engine runs.

terminal.summary: Out of fuel — refueled, engine runs

ge-a17.actionText: WARNING: fuel is explosive — no smoking or open flame. Add the specified diesel fuel (WP 0016, Servicing, Table 1). Restart (WP 0005, Starting Procedures).

ge-q12a.text: Does the generator start and keep running?

ge-a18.actionText: Shut down, let the exhaust cool, and remove the obstruction from the exhaust opening.

ge-q20a.text: Does the generator develop full power now?

ge-t21.text: Exhaust opening was obstructed; cleared and full power restored.

terminal.summary: Exhaust obstruction cleared — full power

gx-q1.text: What color is the exhaust smoke?

gx-q2.text: Is the generator using the correct fuel type listed for the current temperature in TM WP 0016, Table 1 (e.g. DF-2, DF-1, DF-A, JP-8, JP-5)?

gx-q3.text: Is the generator using a fuel listed for the current temperature in TM WP 0016, Table 1?

gx-q4.text: Check the air cleaner restriction indicator (Symptom 9, Step 2). Is the element clogged?

gx-a1.actionText: Service the air cleaner assembly (WP 0014, Servicing). Run the generator and observe the exhaust.

gx-t1.text: Wrong fuel type in the generator. Notify next higher maintenance level to drain and refuel.

terminal.summary: Improper fuel type causing exhaust smoke — needs drain and refuel

gx-t2.text: Blue or white exhaust smoke with correct fuel. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Blue/white exhaust smoke — beyond operator repair

gx-t3.text: Black exhaust smoke after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Black exhaust smoke — beyond operator repair

gx-t4.text: Air cleaner was dirty causing black smoke. Serviced and exhaust is clear.

terminal.summary: Dirty air cleaner caused black smoke — serviced, exhaust clear

gx-q6.text: Check the PERCENT RATED CURRENT ammeter on each phase (Step 3). Is the generator overloaded (over 100%)?

gx-a2.actionText: Reduce the electrical load until the ammeter reads 100% or less on every phase. If unable to adjust, notify the next higher maintenance level.

gx-t5.text: Generator was overloaded; load reduced and black smoke cleared.

terminal.summary: Overload caused black smoke — load reduced

go-q1.text: Oil pressure is low. Check the oil level on the dipstick. Is the oil low?

go-a1.actionText: Shut down. Open the left engine access door, remove the oil filler cap, add oil per LO 9-6115-642-12, install the cap (WP 0018, Servicing). Restart and check oil pressure (25-60 psi).

go-q2.text: Is the coolant temperature high — above 200°F (93°C)? (Step 2)

go-q3.text: Check the coolant level. Is it low?

go-a2.actionText: WARNING: hot coolant/steam can burn. With the engine cool, fill the coolant recovery (overflow) bottle to the COLD line (HOT line if hot) with proper coolant (WP 0015, Servicing, Table 1). Restart and check oil pressure.

go-q4.text: Is the air intake or exhaust obstructed with debris?

go-a3.actionText: Shut down the generator. Clear all debris from the air intake grills, exhaust grills, and surrounding area. Restart and check oil pressure.

go-q5.text: Is the fan belt loose or slipping?

go-t1.text: Oil was low causing low pressure. Oil added, pressure is normal.

terminal.summary: Low oil level — added oil, pressure normal

go-t2.text: Engine was overheating due to low coolant, which caused low oil pressure. Coolant added.

terminal.summary: Low coolant caused overheating/low oil pressure — coolant added

go-t3.text: Air intake was obstructed causing overheating and low oil pressure. Debris removed.

terminal.summary: Air intake obstructed — debris removed, pressure normal

go-t4.text: Fan belt is loose, which may cause overheating and low oil pressure. Notify next higher maintenance level for belt adjustment.

terminal.summary: Loose fan belt — needs maintenance for adjustment

go-t5.text: Low oil pressure after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Low oil pressure — beyond operator repair

gc-q1.text: Coolant temperature indicator shows overheating. Check the ammeter PERCENT RATED CURRENT. Is the generator overloaded (above 100%)?

gc-a1.actionText: Disconnect or turn off enough electrical loads to bring the ammeter PERCENT RATED CURRENT below 100%. Allow the generator to cool down and check the temperature indicator.

gc-q1a.text: Does the temperature come down after reducing load?

gc-q2.text: Check the coolant level. Is it low?

gc-a2.actionText: Shut down and let it cool. Fill the coolant recovery (overflow) bottle to the COLD line with proper coolant (WP 0015, Servicing). Restart and monitor COOLANT TEMP (170-200°F normal).

gc-q3.text: Check the oil level on the dipstick. Is it low?

gc-a3.actionText: Add oil per LO 9-6115-642-12 (WP 0018, Servicing). Run and monitor temperature.

gc-q3a.text: Is the temperature dropping to normal?

gc-q4.text: Is the air intake or exhaust obstructed with debris?

gc-a4.actionText: Shut down the generator. Clear all debris from the air intake grills, exhaust grills, and surrounding area. Restart and monitor the temperature.

gc-q4a.text: Is the temperature dropping to normal?

gc-q5.text: Is the fan belt loose or slipping?

gc-t1.text: Generator was overloaded. Load reduced, temperature returning to normal.

terminal.summary: Generator overloaded — load reduced, temp normal

gc-t2.text: Generator still overheating after reducing load. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Overheating despite load reduction — needs maintenance

gc-t3.text: Coolant was low causing overheating. Coolant added, temperature normal.

terminal.summary: Low coolant — added coolant, temp normal

gc-t4.text: Oil was low contributing to overheating. Oil added, temperature normal.

terminal.summary: Low oil — added oil, temp normal

gc-t5.text: Air intake was obstructed causing overheating. Debris removed, temperature normal.

terminal.summary: Air intake obstructed — debris removed, temp normal

gc-t6.text: Fan belt is loose causing insufficient cooling. Notify next higher maintenance level for belt adjustment.

terminal.summary: Loose fan belt — needs maintenance for adjustment

gc-t7.text: Generator overheating after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Overheating — beyond operator repair

gl-q1.text: What electrical problem are you experiencing?

options.label: Battery not charging or low charge
AC voltmeter shows low voltage or fluctuates
AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER light does not light when switch is closed

gl-q2.text: Check the BATTERY CHARGER FUSE (WP 0004, Table 1, Item 21) (Symptom 12, Step 1). Is it blown?

gl-q3.text: Is the fan belt intact and tight? A loose or broken belt prevents the alternator from charging.

gl-q4.text: Check for loose or broken wires at the back of the battery charging alternator and at the BATTERY CHARGE ammeter. Any problems?

options.label: Yes — loose or broken wires found

gl-q6.text: Check the battery electrolyte level (Symptom 13, Step 1). Is it low (below the bottom of each cap cylinder)?

gl-q7.text: Check the battery connections (Step 2). Are any loose or corroded?

gl-q8.text: Is the AM-VM transfer switch set to match the load connection, and is the VOLTAGE adjust potentiometer set to rated voltage? (Symptom 14, Step 1)

options.label: Set correctly but voltage still low or fluctuating

gl-q9.text: Check for loose or broken wires at the back of the AM-VM transfer switch, VOLTAGE adjust potentiometer, and AC voltmeter. Any found?

gl-q10.text: Press the AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER light to test it (Symptom 18, Step 1). Does it light?

gl-q11.text: Check the load cables for proper connection (WP 0005, Installation of Load Cables) (Step 2). Are they connected correctly?

gl-a2.actionText: Shut down. Connect the load cables per WP 0005, Installation of Load Cables. Restart and close the AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER switch.

gl-q11a.text: Does the AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER light come on now?

gl-q12.text: Does the load exceed the generator rating (PERCENT RATED CURRENT over 100%)? (Step 3)

gl-a3.actionText: Reduce the load below the generator rating, then close the AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER switch.

gl-q12a.text: Does the AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER light come on now?

gl-q14.text: Open the control panel and inspect the circuit breaker on the side of the Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter. Is it tripped, or is the red band visible on the GFCI reset button? (Symptom 19)

gl-a4.actionText: Reset the GFCI side breaker if tripped. If the red band is visible, push the reset button. Check for voltage at the convenience receptacle.

gl-q14a.text: Is there voltage at the convenience receptacle now?

gl-q15.text: On generator sets with contract number DAAK01-88-D-0080 only: check the fuse on the black wire of the GFCI (convenience receptacle). Is it blown?

gl-t1.text: BATTERY CHARGER FUSE is blown. Notify next higher maintenance level for fuse replacement.

terminal.summary: Battery charger fuse blown — needs replacement

gl-t2.text: Fan belt is loose or broken, preventing alternator from charging. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Loose/broken fan belt — battery not charging, needs maintenance

gl-t3.text: Loose or broken wires found. Notify next higher maintenance level for repair.

terminal.summary: Loose/broken wiring — needs maintenance

gl-t4.text: Battery not charging after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Battery not charging — beyond operator repair

gl-t5.text: Battery electrolyte was low; distilled water added and charging is normal.

terminal.summary: Low battery electrolyte — distilled water added, charging normal

gl-t6.text: Excessive battery charging after operator checks. Notify the next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Excessive battery charging — beyond operator repair

gl-t7.text: Loose or corroded battery connections — notify the next higher maintenance level (WP 0009, Symptom 13, Step 2; WP 0013, Servicing, step 7). Do not clean or tighten them yourself. Damaged/loose battery cables are NMC (WP 0011, Table 1, item 18).

terminal.summary: Battery connections loose/corroded — needs maintenance

gl-t8.text: AM-VM transfer switch / VOLTAGE adjust potentiometer set; output voltage is in the rated range.

terminal.summary: Voltage adjusted — output normal

gl-t9.text: AC voltage is low after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Low AC voltage — beyond operator repair

gl-t10.text: AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER light fails the press-to-test. Refer to the next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: AC circuit interrupter light fails test — needs maintenance

gl-t11.text: Load cables were connected incorrectly; corrected and the interrupter closes.

terminal.summary: Load cables reconnected — interrupter closes

gl-t12.text: AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPTER light still does not light with correct connections and load. Refer to the next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: AC circuit interrupter will not close — needs maintenance

gl-t13.text: Generator was overloaded causing the interrupter to trip. Load reduced, running normally.

terminal.summary: Generator overloaded — load reduced, interrupter holds

gl-t14.text: GFCI was tripped. Reset and convenience receptacle has voltage.

terminal.summary: GFCI tripped — reset, receptacle has voltage

gl-t15.text: Convenience receptacle fuse is blown. Notify next higher maintenance level for fuse replacement.

terminal.summary: Convenience receptacle fuse blown — needs replacement

gl-t16.text: No voltage at convenience receptacle after all operator checks. Notify next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: No voltage at receptacle — beyond operator repair

gl-a5.actionText: WARNING: batteries give off flammable gas; acid burns. Shut down, open the engine access door, remove the battery caps, add distilled water to each cell as required (to the bottom of the cap cylinder), replace the caps (WP 0013, Servicing).

gl-q6a.text: After running, is the charging rate normal now?

gl-q16.text: Set the FREQUENCY adjust control (Symptom 15, Step 1). Is the frequency correct and steady now?

gl-q17.text: Check for loose or broken wires at the back of the FREQUENCY adjust control and frequency meter. Any found?

gl-t17.text: Frequency set with the FREQUENCY adjust control.

terminal.summary: Frequency adjusted — correct

gl-t18.text: Frequency off scale or fluctuating with no operator-correctable cause. Notify the next higher maintenance level.

terminal.summary: Frequency off/fluctuating — needs maintenance
